newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian General News - Oct 3.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

U.S. action over what it sees as illegal trade practices by Australia will force Australia's passenger motor vehicle and textile, clothing and footwear assistance plans to go on trial before the World Trade Organisation, posing a threat to 10,000-15,000 jos. Page 1.

Included in the federal government's draft telecommunications post-97 legislation is a plan to allow telecommunications carriers to introduce timed local calls for business users of the Internet and other data-based services. However, the government has backed away from a proposal to tighten untimed local calls for residential users. Page 3.

In the latest of a series of differences between Prime Minister John Howard and Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett, Howard has suggested Kennett take a holiday after the premier predicted a recession. Kennett has also called for an overhaul of Commonwealth-State relations and the introduction of a broad-based tax. Page 4.

In a blow to unions, the New South Wales Industrial Relations Commission has found that federal award employees in New South Wales are unable to claim unfair dismissal under state law. The judgment goes against the views of practitioners, who widely beleved that the state's new Industrial Relations Act extended the state dismissal jurisdiction to federal award employees earning less than A$62,200 a year. Page 4.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Dutch postal and telecoms agency Royal PTT Nederland NV (KPN) yesterday launched a A$2 billion friendly takeover bid for TNT Ltd, acquiring a 9.9 percent stake in the Australian transport group. KPN, the 39th largest company in Europe, could restore the troubled TNT to its former glory, according to TNT managing director David Mortimer. Page 1.

Following a move by the United States yesterday to take action against two of Australia's key export schemes under new world trade rules, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer branded the action "galling". The car and textile industries warned the move could threaten the viability of their industries and endanger thousands of jobs. Page 1.

Despite his calls for health funds to exercise restraint, Prime Minister John Howard has approved further health insurance premium rises. Three National Mutual subsidiaries have been given the go-ahead to increase premiums by an average of 10.3 percent in Western Australia, 8.9 percent in the Northern Territory and 5.1 percent in South Australia. Page 3.

Following Australian Workers Union threats to cancel its affiliation with the Australian Labor Party, New South Wales Premier Bob Carr announced yesterday he would reconsider a more environmentally-friendly re-write of North Ltd's failed A$1.2 billion Lake Cowal gold mine poposal. The development application was rejected five months ago on the grounds North Ltd could not satisfy strict environmental guidelines. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Treasurer Peter Costello sparked a surge on world financial markets yesterday when he revealed that U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Dr Alan Greenspan had told him that inflation was well under control in the United States and there was no need to raise interest rates. Page 1.

According to research conducted at the Women's Health Australia project, based at the universities of Newcastle and Queensland, hysterectomies are more likely in women who do not have access to specialist care, such as women who live in rural and remote aeas, or who may be less likely to question their doctors about alternative treatments. Page 1.

Only 24 hours after the finalisation of the sale of its 50 percent stake in Ansett Australia, the TNT Ltd board has approved a A$2 billion friendly takeover offer from Dutch postal and telecommunications giant Royal PTT Nederland NV (KPN). KPN chairman im Dik said the new company's operations would create a "global force" in the express courier and logistics industry. Page 1.

In an unusual move, the chief judge of the common law division of the New South Wales Supreme Court Justice David Hunt last week transferred four of Justice Vince Bruce's libel cases to other judges. The litigants in the cases have been waiting more than a year for pre-trial rulings - rulings barristers and solicitors believe should have taken a matter of weeks at the most. Page 3.
THE AGE

Treasurer Peter Costello has caused the federal government international embarassment by revealing details of a private conservation on interest rates with U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Dr Alan Greenspan, sending markets in three countries into a flurry of activity and prompting the Opposition to call for Costello's resignation. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard and Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett have clashed again, this time over Kennett's latest comments on the national tax debate, saying the economy requires urgent broad-based tax reform. Howard responded sharply to the statement saying Kennett should take a holiday. Page 1.

Up to A$5 billion in Australian exports and 15,000 local jobs are in jeopardy due to unprecedented trade action by the United States against a Melbourne leather company. The move has prompted federal government and industry criticism, claiming the action is due to the upcoming U.S. presidential election, as President Bill Clinton is attempting to gain favour with U.S. companies. Page 3.

According to U.S. expert Professor Alvin Smith from Oregon State University's Laboratory for Calicivirus Studies, the rabbit killing virus soon to released in Australia will almost certainly infect people. In a letter to Prime Minister John Howard, Smith claims Australia's scientific community has misled the government on the potential impact of the virus. Page 3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
